_source_note: New class built (Sept 2026) from 53 real Ascension screenshots (Runemaster.docx, exact levels/numbers/costs) plus the big CoA handoff doc for structure, spec identity, and passive filler (per Kyle's established two-source pattern: screenshots are authoritative for numbers, handoff doc fills in talent-tree shape and flavor). 3 specs confirmed, no healer/tank: Glyphic (ranged Intellect caster, Arcane Mage analog - glyph-stacking builder/spender), Engravement (Agility melee, Enhancement Shaman analog - weapon-proc weaving), Riftblade (Agility melee, Enhancement/Frost DK hybrid - elemental strike weaving). Mana + Runes dual-resource (Runes = the Frost/Fire/Arcane Glyph-cycle system, already stubbed in combat/abilities.py's ResourceType.RUNES before this session). Cloth armor per the handoff doc's own class header, but base stats hybridized (some Agility) since 2 of 3 specs are melee - see Character.py's Runemaster stat block.

abilities.name: Weapon Engraving: Fire
abilities.description: Engrave a fire rune onto your weapon, granting Fire Engraving: your direct damage has a chance to stack Firebrand on the target, which explodes into Fire damage on expiry. Only one Engraving active.
abilities._source: Confirmed screenshot: Lvl 1, 2 Mana, 'Your direct damage has a 30% chance to apply Firebrand to the target, stacking up to 100 times... When this effect expires, it explodes, dealing 17 Fire damage per stack.' 1hr real duration modeled as 30-min WoW-buff-style per project convention. Stack-and-detonate proc mechanic not fully modeled - see _implementation_note.
abilities._implementation_note: Firebrand is now a real stacking DoT - potency 17 matches the screenshot's '17 Fire damage per stack' exactly, and StatusEffect.tick_potency() multiplies a DoT tick by its stacks (added 2026-10-27; before that a stacking DoT ticked for a bare potency and stacking was purely cosmetic, which is why this shipped as a flat placeholder). The screenshot's 'stacking up to 100 times, explodes on expiry' becomes a 5-stack burn that ticks harder as it builds: 100 stacks assumes a long fight with fast auto-attacks, and this engine is turn-based, so 100 is unreachable and the detonation would never land. Ramps 17 -> 85 per tick instead of a single flat 45.

abilities.name: Weapon Engraving: Ice
abilities.description: Engrave an ice rune onto your weapon, granting Ice Engraving: your direct damage has a chance to deal Frost damage and slow the target, stacking Icebound Momentum for bonus damage. Only one Engraving active.
abilities._source: Confirmed screenshot: Lvl 6, 2 Mana, 'Your direct damage has a 40% chance to deal 14 Frost damage and reduce the target's movement speed by 50% for 8 sec... The Runemaster deals 1% additional damage per stack as Frost damage. Stacks up to 8 times and lasts 12 sec.' Both halves now fire off the one 40% roll via apply_effect's list form (added 2026-10-27 - before that a proc could apply exactly one effect, so this shipped with only the slow and the class's signature ramp was missing). There is no movement speed in a turn-based game, so the 50% slow becomes -15 Haste, which is one of the few stat_mods a Monster actually reads. Icebound Momentum is the 1%-per-stack damage ramp, 8 stacks as per the screenshot.

abilities.name: Weapon Engraving: Earth
abilities.description: Engrave an earth rune onto your weapon, granting Earth Engraving: your direct damage has a chance to deal Nature damage to nearby enemies. Only one Engraving active.
abilities._source: Confirmed screenshot: Lvl 14, 2 Mana, 'Your direct damage has a 15% chance to deal 1 Nature damage to enemies within 8 yds of your target.' The actual splash is now real, via the splash_damage proc payload (added 2026-10-27 as the mirror of splash_heal). This engine has no AoE radius, so 'within 8 yds of your target' becomes 'the other enemies in this fight', capped at 3 and excluding the enemy that took the original hit. 25% of the triggering damage rather than the screenshot's flat 1, which is a level-1-scaled number that would be invisible at 60. The armour shred is kept as a rider: it was all this ability had before, and it is one of the few debuffs a Monster reads.

abilities.name: Palm Sigil: Earth
abilities.description: Engrave an earth rune into your palm: your next Magic damage stuns the target. Usable while moving.
abilities._source: Confirmed screenshot: Lvl 8, 'your next instance of direct Magic damage within 6 sec stuns a target enemy for 4 sec.' Part of the Palm Sigil family.  THE STUN NEVER HAPPENED. The description is 'your next Magic damage stuns the target' and the ability carried no stun of any kind - not is_stun, which would have been wrong anyway (this is a DEFERRED stun on a later cast, not a stun on this one), and no proc. Now a 100% on_damage_cast proc that lands a 1-turn is_stun debuff on the target, which is the shape the description describes. StatusEffect accepts is_stun and apply_effect passes it through.

abilities.name: Ley Lock

abilities._source: Confirmed screenshot: Lvl 18, 'preventing any spell in that school from being cast for 2.50 sec.' Real hard interrupt shared across all 3 specs per the handoff doc.  Removed dead flag stat_mod(s) ['silenced']: nothing in the engine reads them. The real mechanism is the ability-level is_stun flag, which this ability already carries. Keeping them was the is_aoe trap waiting to happen: data that looks like the mechanism and is not. This engine has exactly one incapacitate mechanic, is_stun, with no separate silence or root category (see StatusEffect.is_stun).

abilities.name: Weapon Engraving: Air
abilities.description: Engrave an air rune onto your weapon, granting Air Engraving: increases attack/cast speed, and your direct damage has a chance to replicate a % of the damage, ignoring Armor. Only one Engraving active.
abilities._source: Confirmed screenshot: Lvl 24, 2 Mana, '+10% melee, ranged, and spell casting speed. Your direct damage has a 15% chance to replicate 30% of the damage dealt. Replicated damage ignores armor.' The haste half always worked - this was the only Engraving with real stat_mods - but the replicate half was simply absent, so the second sentence of its own tooltip did nothing. bonus_pct is the exact mechanic: it adds a fraction of the triggering hit to that same hit rather than rolling a phantom follow-up attack, and because it is added after the original hit has already been through armour it inherently ignores armour, matching 'replicated damage ignores armor' without needing a separate penetration path.

abilities.name: Weapon Engraving: Water
abilities.description: Engrave a water rune onto your weapon, granting Water Engraving: your direct damage has a chance to drain mana and deal Frost damage, also granting nearby allies Replenishment. Only one Engraving active.
abilities._source: Confirmed screenshot: Lvl 26, 2 Mana, 'Your direct damage has a 30% chance to drain up to 2% of your maximum mana from the target, restoring the amount drained and dealing Frost damage based on how much mana was drained. Also grants nearby allies Replenishment: Replenishes 5% of maximum mana per 5 sec for 15 sec.' The mana return is grant_resource; the 'Frost damage based on how much mana was drained' is bonus_pct 0.15 on the same hit, since a drain of a fixed 2% always converts to the same damage anyway and most monsters here have no mana pool to drain from. The ally Replenishment is NOT modelled: there is no party-wide resource payload (splash_heal spreads healing, not mana) and on_target false reaches only the caster. That is the one part of this tooltip still unbuilt - it needs a splash_resource payload.

Real numbers not confirmed via a dedicated screenshot. damage_taken_pct in a status stat_mod is a FRACTION: character.py's take_damage adds get_status_stat_mod('damage_taken_pct') to taken_mult undivided, while physical_damage_taken_pct and magic_damage_taken_pct four lines below it in the same method are divided by 100. abilities.description: Reduces damage taken and increases maximum Mana. Only one Aspect active.
abilities._source: CoA handoff doc: 'Reduces damage taken; boosts max mana. One Aspect active.' Real numbers not confirmed via a dedicated screenshot. damage_taken_pct in a status stat_mod is a FRACTION: character.py's take_damage adds get_status_stat_mod('damage_taken_pct') to taken_mult undivided, while physical_damage_taken_pct and magic_damage_taken_pct four lines below it in the same method are divided by 100. The convention is per key with no naming rule, so do not generalise from either one. This was -8, which is -800%: it clamped every hit to 1 damage and made a 30-turn stance a flat immunity.  max_mana_pct IS A FRACTION, NOT PERCENT POINTS. This was 10, i.e. 1000%. It was invisible until the effect_value-0 fix made this buff apply at all - 113 buffs across seven classes were multiplying their own stat_mods by zero, so a latent unit error in one of them did nothing either. Bringing dead content to life is exactly when you re-measure: Guardian Vanguard's effective HP jumped from ~3,270 to 26,571 and its survival to 577 turns against peers at 6-23. Verified: max_health_pct 0.08 takes 532 health to 574, 8.0 takes it to 4,788.
